World of Warcraft Forums

# Showing Elements in Combat Lockdown

Guides UI and Macro

[Rylak-3034442](https://us.forums.blizzard.com/en/wow/u/Rylak-3034442) (Rylak) August 18, 2020, 3:30am 1

Hi everyone,

Taints have recently become a bit of an issue in my addon and I believe that the cause is showing/hiding UI addon-generated elements such as frames and buttons during combat.  
I understand that Show/HideUIPanel is now a protected function and cannot be used during combat lockdown as of 8.2.0, but could anyone please confirm if frame:Show() has the same restrictions?  
I assume that :Show() is called from within ShowUIPanel so I’m guessing that the answer would be yes.

How do you personally work around this combat restriction? I maintain a loot distribution addon so a lot of the time loot will be distributed while the rest of the raid continues to clear so combat lockdown will regularly be a concern.

[Gello-89115](https://us.forums.blizzard.
com/en/wow/u/Gello-89115) (Gello) August 18, 2020, 3:40am 2

If a frame contains secure elements then Show/Hide are protected in combat yes.

What’s the criteria for showing/hiding? Do you just want to show/hide in response to a macro or keybind? (doable) or some event? (less likely)

And what are you trying to show? A part of the default UI? Or an addon’s window? Many default UI elements you can show by /click to a button that summons the window.

[Rylak-3034442](https://us.forums.blizzard.com/en/wow/u/Rylak-3034442) (Rylak) August 18, 2020, 3:45am 3

(Same guy as OP, just changed character)

> If a frame contains secure elements then Show/Hide are protected in combat yes.
> 
> 

So I’m a little bit iffy on that. 100% of what the addon shows/hides has been produced by the addon but I understand that anything anchored to a protected frame itself becomes protected.

>

[Gello-89115](https://us.forums.blizzard.com/en/wow/u/Gello-89115) (Gello) August 18, 2020, 10:30am 4

For an addon that only deals with loot and doesn’t use any items (or any part of the default UI that would be secure), I would probably see about finding what’s secure and modifying that so it’s no longer secure.
Once you start using secure frames you’re bound by its rules and you’ll start to get into arcana that may be overkill for what you’re after.

If you have a button that inherits SecureActionButtonTemplate and parent it to a very basic frame, that parent frame is now protected and its parent up the chain.

Here’s a pair of frames where the parent frame (Fr1) has a “Click Me” button that shows a child frame (Fr2) that contains a secure button (pet heal) the traditional way:

```
-- main frame is not protected yet
local f1 = Fr1 or CreateFrame("Frame", "Fr1", UIParent, "BasicFrameTemplate")
f1:SetSize(200,200)
f1:SetPoint("CENTER")

-- child of f1, so far unsecure too
local f2 = Fr2 or CreateFrame("Frame", "Fr2", Fr1, "BasicFrameTemplate")
f2:SetSize(200,200)
--f2:SetPoint("RIGHT",f1,"LEFT")
f2:SetPoint("CENTER",-300,0)
f2:Hide()

-- child of f1 too, "Click Me" button that shows f2
local b1 = Bt1 or CreateFrame("Button", "Bt1", Fr1, "UIPanelButtonTemplate")
b1:SetWidth(80)
b1:SetPoint("CENTER")
b1:SetText("Click Me")
b1:SetScript("OnClick",function(self) f2:Show() end)

-- up to this point, above works in or out of combat

-- adding this button to heal battle pets to f2 now makes f2 protected, and ALSO f1. everything up the parent chain gets protected
local b2 = Bt2 or CreateFrame("ItemButton", "Bt2", Fr2, "SecureActionButtonTemplate")
b2:SetPoint("CENTER")
b2.icon:SetTexture(644389)
b2:SetAttribute("type","spell")
b2:SetAttribute("spell","Revive Battle Pets")

-- so now you can't show either of the frames in combat with /run Fr1:Show() or Fr2:Show()
```

As mentioned in the comments, adding that secure button now makes both Fr2 and Fr1 protected and they can’t be shown in combat with frame:Show().

Now you’ve entered the secure environment and want to manipulate your frames securely. First we’ll make the Click Me button inherit SecureHandlerClickTemplate:
`local b1 = Bt1 or CreateFrame(“Button”, “Bt1”, Fr1, “UIPanelButtonTemplate,SecureHandlerClickTemplate”)`  
and we’ll replace this:  
`b1:SetScript(“OnClick”,function(self) f2:Show() end)`  
with this:  
`b1:SetFrameRef(“Fr2”,Fr2)  
b1:SetAttribute(“_onclick”,[[ self:GetFrameRef(“Fr2”):Show() ]])`

b1 (the “Click Me” button) will show Fr2 from the secure environment. (There are various ways of doing this btw.)

```
-- main frame is not protected yet
local f1 = Fr1 or CreateFrame("Frame", "Fr1", UIParent, "BasicFrameTemplate")
f1:SetSize(200,200)
f1:SetPoint("CENTER")

-- child of f1, so far unsecure too
local f2 = Fr2 or CreateFrame("Frame", "Fr2", Fr1, "BasicFrameTemplate")
f2:SetSize(200,200)
f2:SetPoint("RIGHT",f1,"LEFT")
f2:Hide()

-- child of f1 too, "Click Me" button that shows f2
local b1 = Bt1 or CreateFrame("Button", "Bt1", Fr1, "UIPanelButtonTemplate,SecureHandlerClickTemplate")
b1:SetSize(80,24)
b1:SetPoint("CENTER")
b1:SetText("Click Me")
-- your new OnClick is a secure _click snippet, and it needs to know what it will show beforehand; here by creating a frame reference
b1:SetFrameRef("Fr2",Fr2)
b1:SetAttribute("_onclick",[[ self:GetFrameRef("Fr2"):Show() ]])

-- adding this button to heal battle pets to f2 now makes f2 protected, and ALSO f1. everything up the parent chain gets protected
local b2 = Bt2 or CreateFrame("ItemButton", "Bt2", Fr2, "SecureActionButtonTemplate")
b2:SetPoint("CENTER")
b2.icon:SetTexture(644389)
b2:SetAttribute("type","spell")
b2:SetAttribute("spell","Revive Battle Pets")

-- now the Click Me button will show Fr2 in combat
```

Now to show Fr1 you’ll need to use a secure method too, which can be a click key binding or a secure button bound to a key or other methods.

Recommended reading include the secure execution stuff on wowpedia:

[Wowpedia](https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Secure_Execution_and_Tainting)

### [Secure Execution and Tainting](https://wowpedia.fandom.
com/wiki/Secure_Execution_and_Tainting)

The User Interface API mandates human decision-making, particularly in combat, by protecting many functions from insecure or tainted use. This security model was largely introduced in Patch 2.0[1] and has been a cornerstone of the API ever since.

And of course the authoritave reference for the secure environment from Iriel:  
<http://www.iriel.org/wow/docs/SecureHeadersGuide-4.0-r1.pdf>

excerpts: boolean - If true, the call will allow non-"full"/non-"center" area frames to replace existing "full"/"center" frames (by forcibly closing those "blocking" frames); otherwise those would prevent all "ShowUIPanel" calls for "lesser" frames" until such high-priority frames are manually closed. This flag isn't necessary if you want to replace a "full" area frame with another "full" frame, or likewise with "center" frames. It's only necessary if you want to forcibly replace such high-priority frames with things like "left"/"doublewide"-area frames instead (which have lower priorities). These functions can only be called from secure (Blizzard) code, or from addon code in response to a hardware event (keypress or mouse click) while **not** in combat.

Protected Functions

The following functions are protected and cannot be called freely from addon code:

|Function |Purpose |
| --- | --- |
|`CastSpellByName()` |Cast a spell by name |
|`TargetUnit()` |Target a specific unit |
|`UseAction()` |Use an action bar slot |
|`JumpOrAscendStart()` |Make the character jump |
|`ToggleAutoRun()` |Toggle auto-run |
|`StartAttack()` |Begin auto-attack |
|`PetAttack()` |Command pet to attack |
|`RunMacroText()` |Execute macro text |
|`SetBinding()` |Set a key binding |

These require a **hardware event** (real user input) and are fully blocked during combat lockdown.

## Taint System ¶

The taint system is Blizzard's mechanism for tracking which code and data originate from addons versus the default UI. This prevents addon code from interfering with secure Blizzard UI operations.
For full technical details, see the [Secure Execution and Tainting](https://warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Secure_Execution_and_Tainting) article on the Warcraft wiki.

### Secure vs. Tainted Code ¶

* **Secure code** — Blizzard's default UI code. It can call protected functions and modify secure frames.
* **Tainted code** — Any code originating from an addon. It cannot call protected functions during combat.

### How Taint Propagates ¶

Taint spreads through execution like a virus:

1. Reading a **tainted variable** taints the current execution path
2. A tainted execution path **taints any variables it writes**
3. Any function called from a tainted path becomes tainted

```
-- Example: taint propagation  local secureValue = SomeSecureFunction () -- secure  local taintedValue = MyAddonVariable -- tainted (addon-created)   -- Reading taintedValue taints this execution path  local result = secureValue + taintedValue -- result is now TAINTED   -- This would fail if called during combat from a tainted path  -- TargetUnit("player")  -- ERROR: blocked by taint
```

Irrevocable Taint

Calling `loadstring()` or `setfenv()` **irrevocably taints** the resulting code. There is no way to "untaint" code produced by these functions. Avoid them if your code needs to interact with secure frames.

### Checking Taint Status ¶

Use `issecurevariable()` to inspect whether a variable is tainted:

```
 local isTainted = not issecurevariable ( "SomeGlobalVariable" )  if isTainted then  print ( "SomeGlobalVariable is tainted by addon code" )  end   -- Check a table field  local isTainted = not issecurevariable ( SomeTable , "key" )
```

## Combat Lockdown ¶
During combat, Blizzard locks down the secure UI environment. This is the most common source of addon errors for new developers.

### Detecting Combat Lockdown ¶

```
 if InCombatLockdown () then  print ( "In combat — protected actions are blocked!" )  end
```

During Combat Lockdown, You Cannot:

* Call **any** protected function
* Create new **secure frames** (frames using secure templates)
* Modify **secure frame attributes** (e.g., changing a SecureActionButton's action)
* Show or hide **secure frames**

### Pattern: Queue Actions for After Combat ¶

The standard pattern is to queue desired actions during combat and execute them when combat ends via the `PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED` event:

```
 local addonName , ns = ...   ns . pendingActions = {}   local frame = CreateFrame ( "Frame" )  frame : RegisterEvent ( "PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED" )   frame : SetScript ( "OnEvent" , function ( self , event )  if event == "PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED" then  for _ , action in ipairs ( ns .

...

* **No filesystem access** — Cannot read, write, or list files (SavedVariables are the only persistence mechanism, managed by the game client)
* **No network access** — Cannot open sockets, make HTTP requests, or communicate outside the game (addon messages are the only inter-player communication)
* **No system commands** — Cannot execute OS commands, launch processes, or interact with the operating system
* **No gameplay automation** — Cannot cast spells, target units, use items, or move the character without a real hardware event
* **No secure frame modification in combat** — Cannot show, hide, or change attributes on secure frames during combat lockdown
* **No cross-addon SavedVariables** — Cannot directly read another addon's saved data (use addon messages or public APIs instead)
* **No raw memory access** — Cannot read or modify game memory; only the exposed Lua API is available

## Best Practices ¶
